label: Point Nemo, open South Pacific, AD 1500

location.modernLabel: Oceanic Pole of Inaccessibility, Point Nemo
location.coordinateMeaning: A sea-surface aperture at the ocean coordinate farthest from land, not a vessel, island, seabed, or fixed human site.

temporal.localTimeInput: 12:00 local solar hour, calendar day and season unspecified
temporal.supportedResolution: Open-ocean geography and broad preindustrial material boundary only.
temporal.precisionBoundary: No source reconstructs exact local weather, waves, visibility, biology, or vessel presence at this coordinate and year.

habitation.evidence: The coordinate is open ocean thousands of kilometres from land and has no permanent built habitation.
habitation.qualification: This is the expected spatial class for an ordinary frame, not proof that no voyaging vessel ever crossed the exact point at an exact instant.

viewpoint.support: An unsupported wormhole aperture just above the sea surface.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: Point Nemo is the ocean location farthest from land, about 2688 kilometres from its nearest land points.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The horizon remains open water in every direction; land, reef, beach, and coastal vegetation do not belong.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The coordinate lies over deep South Pacific ocean rather than visible shallow bottom.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The seafloor and reef structure cannot appear in a surface view.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: East Polynesian ocean voyaging existed before AD 1500, but regional archaeology cannot place or exclude a vessel at Point Nemo at one instant.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: A vessel is possible in the abstract but unsupported in the default scene; the card must not convert uncertainty into either telemetry or spectacle.

obligations: Use only sea surface, horizon, sky, wind, waves, light, and defensible open-ocean atmosphere.
Declare the optic as virtual rather than inventing support.
Give the scene an event in water, cloud, or light without manufacturing a datable object.
Keep exact AD 1500 weather and animal presence explicitly uncertain.
oracleOnlyContradictions: An island, reef, beach, coastline, or visible seabed contradicts the coordinate.
A ship, canoe, whale, albatross, plastic, or spacecraft debris is not established at the unspecified instant.
Point Nemo's nearest-land distance is metadata, not a visible marker.
The absence or presence of a vessel cannot be proven from regional voyaging chronology.

sources.title: NOAA Ocean Service - Where is Point Nemo?
High-precision radiocarbon dating of East Polynesian settlement
supports: regional East Polynesian settlement and voyaging chronology

uncertainty: Exact AD 1500 weather, cloud, wave state, sea-surface temperature, and visibility.
Vessel, bird, marine mammal, plankton, and flotsam presence.
Exact local bathymetric depth until the authoritative grid is queried.

review.notes: NOAA geography was checked directly. The card deliberately preserves vessel and weather uncertainty.
